text:
maya: quick note — experimenting with adding a small 'tier hint' to the region selector so premium customers bias to low-latency regions, but still allow fallback to cheaper variants if capacity is constrained. curious about edge cases.

liam: cool, do you mean this as a hard pin or a soft bias? soft sounds safer so we don't create hotspots.

maya: soft bias. plan is probe-weighted scoring: score = w_latency * latency_rank + w_quota * quota_headroom + w_cost * cost_score + tier_bonus. tier_bonus is +0.15 for premium.

sasha: watch out for oscillation when we flip variants during transient spikes. we should add hysteresis and a cooldown per-tenant. e.g., if we fallback once, don't flip back for 30s unless latency improves by >20%.

oliver: agreed on cooldown. also telemetry point — add a tag in traces: region_decision={region,score,variant_reason}. that'll help the dashboard group by reason.

maya: example config I'm prototyping:
```
routing:
  probes:
    latency_weight: 0.6
    quota_weight: 0.25
    cost_weight: 0.15
  tier_bonus:
    premium: 0.15
    standard: 0.0
  cooldown_seconds: 30
  fallback_policy: "variant-first"  # try cheaper quantized variant before cross-region
```

liam: small question — for "variant-first" fallback do we need to verify model-compatibility? some models don't have quantized equivalents. we should consult model-catalog metadata.

sasha: yep add a compatibility check step. also add a per-tenant override flag so some customers can opt out of cross-region fallback for data residency. (cc @oliver)

oliver: +1. UI note: in Console routing page show a mini timeline of recent region swaps and the triggering metric (latency/probe/quota). makes postmortems much faster.

maya: good. on quotas: if customer is near commit for Dedicated, we should prefer their reserved region even if latency is slightly worse. that's another priority bump.

liam: maybe implement priority as additive scores with clamping. also we need experiments to tune weights; can we ship a server-side flag to flip weights per cohort?

deploy-bot: deploy queued: routing-service v2.4.1 -> canary in us-west-2 (maya's experiment flags enabled)

maya: thanks. plan: canary 1h, collect: region_choice histogram, variant_fallback_count, latency_p99_by_region, and rollback if p99 increases >10% for premium. will post results.

sasha: one last thought — circuit-breaker for variant explosion: if more than 5% of traffic for a region falls back in 1m, mark region degraded and steer traffic to next-best. avoids cascading overload.

liam: sounds good. i'll add telemetry buckets and a dashboard with those signals.

maya: perfect. i'll follow up with the rollout playbook and a short Console mock for the timeline widget. thanks all. :thumbsup:
